prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Meridian Regional ATFM+A-CDM; airports Meridian International(=Meridian Regional Airport), Harbor East, North Valley, Lakeside Regional, Southport. Modes (Airport Duty Manager declares from tactical header after coordination; Business Rules Registry then supplies alert/approval/publication thresholds): Normal Operations(minor sequence shift, delay upstream not airborne); Adverse Weather(more tactical reviews); Capacity Reduction State(ADM+Tower Supervisor extend metering horizon; RFM may combine arrival regulation+departure metering for recovery gates); Recovery Phase(Copperfin-approved; RFM authorizes exit); Contingency Fallback; Slot Compliance State; Winter(MBO confirms in Digital Briefing Room; CAM cuts departure capacity). Actors: Regional Flow Manager(RFM; landing-rate reductions; staged increase only after Tower Sequence Manager confirms stable spacing), Airspace Sector Planner(monitors via Sector Load Monitor, confirms en route compatibility), Military Airspace Liaison(flags release/closure assumptions for review), Tower Supervisor(confirms landing rate; North/South Runway Meter; Quartzline pad releases), Airport Duty Manager, Ramp Control Lead, Aircraft Operator Representative+Airline Operations Coordinator(review timing in shared timeline), Slot Coordinator, Network Operations Liaison, Emergency Response Coordinator, Deicing Coordinator, Ground Handling Dispatcher(uses Handling Resource Planner view: off-block demand vs stand servicing), Meteorology Briefing Officer=MBO(verifies Weather Ingest Gateway impacts before capacity applied). Halcyon logs push rationale. Cedarbell=Regional Flow Platform. Parts: Integrated Tactical Management Position; Marlinstone=Demand Prediction Service(forecasts from Flight Intent Message stream+history; triggers regulation when demand>Airport Acceptance Rate); Capacity Assessment Module=CAM(recalcs on runway config/weather/staffing/sector load change); Blueharbor=Slot Allocation Engine(CTT; Ground Delay Program; produces Pushback Window Token when departure window frozen); Foxglove=Airport CDM Portal(TOBT+remarks read-only unless coordination role; acks); Emberline=Departure Metering Service(revised advisories when queue threshold exceeded; CTT→Ironleaf=Tower Sequence Manager); Skylark(apron movement layer refresh ≤5s after validated surface event); Nightjar=Arrival Regulation Console; Gate Conflict Detector; Alert Distribution Hub(routes Tactical Regulation Proposal for acks); accepted→CTT updates/Slot Compliance changes/capacity annotations; all actions, recommendations, acks, rejected alternatives→Collaborative Decision Log+Audit Event Ledger; Performance Analytics Warehouse; Sector Load Monitor; Weather Ingest Gateway; Business Rules

New part:
S443: Surface constraints are treated as tactical capacity inputs because they can change the feasible order, timing, and routing of aircraft after demand has already been balanced against airspace capacity.
S444: The Regional Flow Platform correlates surface equipment conditions with flight intent, stand assignment, and runway plan data before recommending any change to the active tactical plan.
S445: The Surface Surveillance Adapter provides current movement area occupancy and equipment status indicators to the Ramp Movement Board and the Tower Sequence Manager.
S446: When a gate bridge, ground power unit, fuel hydrant point, or marked taxilane is unavailable, the Ramp Control Lead verifies whether the condition blocks a single movement, a stand group, or a wider apron route.
S447: The Airport Duty Manager records the operational significance of the condition in the Airport CDM Portal so that all planning components use the same constraint description.
S448: The Capacity Assessment Module converts persistent surface constraints into reduced stand throughput, extended turn buffers, or modified taxi-out assumptions.
S449: Fuel vehicle holds affect the tactical plan by delaying off-block readiness even when crew, passengers, and aircraft serviceability are otherwise complete.
S450: Tower Sequence Manager uses the hold advice to prevent a departure from being sequenced ahead of a fueling constraint that is still active.
S451: The Airline Operations Coordinator remains responsible for confirming whether the affected flight should keep its Target Off Block Time, request a new value, or accept a later Calculated Takeoff Time.
S452: Airline Interface Adapter produces the Late Baggage Tag List when baggage reconciliation data indicates that departure readiness may be overstated.
S453: Runway metering advisories are applied when the departure queue, runway crossing demand, or runway occupancy trend indicates that uncontrolled pushback would create an unstable surface queue.
S454: North Runway Meter reduces the departure release rate when surface surveillance shows that runway-entry queues are approaching the metering threshold.
S455: The South Runway Meter applies the same planning principle to its assigned runway stream while preserving separation from arrival regulation actions.
S456: The Departure Metering Service translates runway metering limits into candidate pushback spacing for the Slot Allocation Engine.
S457: If the metering action affects a regulated flight, the Slot Coordinator reviews the relationship between the Calculated Takeoff Time and the proposed surface release time before accepting the change.
S458: Apron congestion advisories are generated when the Ramp Movement Board shows conflicting pushbacks, blocked lead-in lines, saturated holding points, or insufficient room for safe wingtip clearance.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
